review.title: Four Stones on the Second Line
review.summary: The 20k won by resignation after 29 moves. GPT-6.1 Sol started level, but C5 on turn 6 swung the lead to Black by 11.1 points, and a run of small-group moves along the bottom edge never gave it back. Both sides blundered heavily: GPT-6.1 Sol averaged 9.6 points lost per move, the 20k 6.5, but the 20k's mistakes were smaller where it counted and the lead stayed with Black.

moments.text: Black's lead was +0.1 and the game was even. GPT-6.1 Sol played C5, which lost 11.0 points and pushed the lead to +11.1. The engine preferred D7, the move that would have kept White's stones from being pressed down toward the left.

After the 20k's E5 gave back 4.8 points, GPT-6.1 Sol replied with E6 and lost 9.6, sending the lead from +6.3 to +15.9. D7 was again the engine's choice, and the chance to take the upper side was gone.
The 20k found a moment of bite: E3 lost 13.1 points, but it was a gift in the wrong direction, cutting the lead from +23.8 to +10.7. The engine wanted C7, and White briefly had real chances.

GPT-6.1 Sol answered with F2, a 19.9-point loss that took the lead from +10.6 to +30.5. The engine's choice was F7, up in the open, rather than crawling along the second line while Black's wall stood over the centre.

G2 was the worst move of the game, losing 27.1 points and moving the lead from +6.4 to +33.5. The 20k had just lost 21.0 with J3, so White was back in the game, and then handed everything straight back; the engine preferred B7.

audit.reason: Everything it ran was board parsing and chain/liberty inspection (the inspect/selected functions in game-188-inspector.js), the one-move capture and liberty check for a named move, a replay of the actual record into SGF, and note writing. None of it looped over empty points to score moves or looked ahead along any line of play, so every choice was made by the player.
